# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Sawyer Foster**
[Street Address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield
Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination**

- **Member name:** Sawyer Foster
- **Member ID:** W558551284
- **Reference number:** POC-64107D6EF7-65599
- **Date of denial notice:** August 1, 2026
- **Service denied:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Plan/Product:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield, Commercial/ACA, New Hampshire
- **Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon)*, https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of my total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which Anthem denied on August 1, 2026 under reference number POC-64107D6EF7-65599. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking for reconsideration, because the records in my chart address the plan's own published criteria directly, and I am asking that they be reviewed against those criteria point by point.

I am appealing under the plan's *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon)*, which is the policy I am quoting throughout this letter. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

The guideline states:

> "ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved Total ankle arthroplasty may also be indicated for revision of failed previous reconstructions where sufficient bone stock and soft tissue integrity are present."

Here is how each element lines up with what is already in my medical record.

**1. Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.**
Weight-bearing ankle radiographs taken on June 5, 2026 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. This is an imaging study of the tibiotalar joint, and the findings are the findings the criterion describes. If the images themselves were not received with the original request, I am asking that they be obtained from [imaging facility name] and reviewed.

**2. Significant pain and functional impairment persisting after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management.**
My symptoms have lasted 18 months — progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. My conservative care includes:

- Supervised physical therapy for ankle strengthening and balance, 14 weeks, from March 9, 2026 to June 15, 2026, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 16, 2026, which gave about 4 weeks of partial relief.

Fourteen weeks of supervised physical therapy exceeds the three months the criterion asks for, and my pain and limitations persisted after it.

The guideline also defines what counts as significant:

> "For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

On the functional side, my chart documents that I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. So that the reviewer has the exact figures the definition calls for, I am asking my surgeon's office to supply my recorded VAS pain score of [VAS rating from office note] on [date of office note] and the specific daily activities listed as impacted in that note: [activities as documented]. If those entries were not in the original packet, that is exactly the kind of gap I am asking to have filled rather than treated as an absence of need.

**3. Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion.**
The criterion gives strong, palpable pedal pulses as its example. My pedal pulse examination is recorded in my surgeon's pre-operative note of [date of vascular/pre-operative exam], and I am asking Dr. Okafor's office to forward that note, along with [any vascular study, if one was performed], so this element can be confirmed from the chart.

**4. Device is FDA approved.**
The implant Dr. Okafor has planned is [implant manufacturer and model], and I am asking that his office confirm its FDA-approved status in writing for the file.

The revision provisions of the guideline, including the section that begins "21 Revision Total Ankle Arthroplasty Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:", do not apply to me, because this is a primary procedure rather than a revision of a previous reconstruction.

## On conservative management specifically

The guideline describes what conservative management should include:

> "Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:"

> "• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

I meet the second half of this on the face of my record: I completed 4 months of anti-inflammatory medication and received a corticosteroid injection on May 16, 2026, and I attended 18 of my prescribed physical therapy visits over 14 weeks, which demonstrates compliance with the plan of therapy. As to footwear modification or accommodative devices, I am asking my treating providers to supply the records of [footwear modification / orthosis trial, with dates, if prescribed]. The guideline also provides that "If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented." and that "If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approa ch is not reasonable." — if any element was not appropriate in my case, I am asking that Dr. Okafor's documentation on that point be reviewed.

I would also note, for the record, that I am a non-smoker, my BMI is 29, and I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. The guideline addresses these kinds of factors in its recommendations, including that "Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended." and that "Where there are patient-specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient a shared decision-making process with the patient to discuss these modifiable comorbidities is strongly recommended and should be documented."

## Why I am asking for a full reconsideration

The denial was not based on a finding that ankle replacement is inappropriate for my condition. It was based on the documentation being incomplete. The plan's own guideline states:

> "Carelon applies objective and evidence-based criteria, and takes individual circumstances and the local delivery system into account when determining the medical appropriateness of health care services."

> "These criteria are designed to guide both providers and reviewers to the most appropriate services based on a patient's unique circumstances."

My individual circumstances are 18 months of progressive, rest-unrelieved ankle pain; radiographic tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts; 14 weeks and 18 visits of supervised physical therapy; 4 months of NSAIDs; a steroid injection that helped for about four weeks; an antalgic gait; and walking limited to two blocks. Where a specific document was missing from the submitted packet, I have identified it above and I am working with my surgeon's office to supply it with this appeal rather than leaving it unaddressed.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask that Anthem:

1. Overturn the denial of CPT 27702 and authorize the total ankle replacement recommended by Dr. Okafor; or
2. If any element remains unresolved, identify in writing the specific document or data point still needed, so that it can be supplied promptly; and
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with orthopedic surgery expertise.

Please send your written determination to me at the address above, and to Dr. Okafor's office. I am also requesting a free copy of the complete claim file, the clinical criteria applied to my request, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the initial determination.

## Submission and deadline

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, **by January 28, 2027**. I am submitting this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which is the authoritative address for my plan. Anthem (Elevance) appeal addresses are state- and plan-specific; members can also log in at anthem.com or use the Sydney Health app, or call the number on the back of the member ID card, but the address printed on the denial letter is the one I am using here.

## Enclosures

- Copy of the denial notice dated August 1, 2026 (reference POC-64107D6EF7-65599)
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report, June 5, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (March 9, 2026 – June 15, 2026, 18 visits)
- Office notes from Okafor, MD, including pain scores and functional limitations
- Medication history and corticosteroid injection record, May 16, 2026
- [Pre-operative vascular/pedal pulse documentation]
- [Implant FDA-approval confirmation]
- [Any other records listed above]

---

Sincerely,

**Sawyer Foster**
Member ID: W558551284
[Signature]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
